observations.body: Hebrews links Jesus’ suffering outside the gate with bodies burned outside the camp, calls readers to go to him, and names praise and generosity as sacrifices.
observations.label: Outside the camp leads to praise and shared goods

observations.body: The passage presents altar, outside camp, disgrace, lasting city, praise, confession, doing good, and sharing as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: altar, outside camp, disgrace, lasting city, praise, confession, doing good, and sharing

observations.body: The passage places outside camp and response beside altar, outside camp, disgrace, lasting city, praise, confession, doing good, and sharing.
observations.label: outside camp and response

payload.posture: Read Hebrews 13:10–16 as evidence about sacrifice, keeping its action, claim, context, and limits distinct.
payload.tension: praise and generosity are named sacrifices without becoming substitutes for Jesus’ suffering
payload.title: Outside the camp leads to praise and shared goods
